raw_images.role: global warm softly lit cartoon style reference

original: The original reads as a rectilinear blue wreck panel with a taller dark terminus on the right, two narrow upright ribs, two square front plates and four small pale rivets.
The two large blue regions are visually broad and largely uninterrupted. Thin dark horizontal separations and a darker band divide them, while the overall edges remain straight and mechanical.
Volume is mostly expressed by dark side faces and abrupt color shifts. The top blue face is bright and saturated; the lower region and lower brace ends become very dark.
The original rivets and plates are small compared with the broad blue areas. Wear, plank grain, broken ends and surface dents are not visibly developed in this snapshot.
fixed_target: The fixed target preserves the recognizable blue wreck-panel identity, dark grey-blue metal construction, paired front ribs and plates, pale round fasteners, two short upper nubs and taller right terminus.

Its blue structure is expressed as multiple irregular horizontal boards with thick rounded edges, staggered seams, visible chips, tapered breaks and shallow longitudinal wear. The upper portion has broad visible top-facing surfaces.
The metal ribs, plates and right terminus have fuller rounded corners and clearer thickness. The target includes a broad horizontal dark band with visible fasteners across it.

The target has strong cool cyan-to-blue surface variation, slate-blue metal, pale cream fasteners, warm yellow edge accents and dark blue recesses. Broad surface gradients make the parts feel fuller than the flat original.
The target contains cracks and localized scratches on metal and wood, with warm glints concentrated near raised corners. Some of its edge highlights are quite sharp and shiny.

The target and original have different image dimensions and visible internal composition. These pixels establish an aesthetic comparison, not a camera, crop, world-size, contact or registration contract.
global_style_reference: The global style image shows a saturated green plant in an orange square pot, with broad controlled shading, warm illuminated top rims, dark but legible recesses and rounded substantial pot corners.
The leaves retain deliberate planar facets while their large surfaces use soft gradients. The pot has broad simple faces and a small number of clearly readable edge transitions.
The global reference is visually quieter than the wreck target: fewer small scratches and less dense bright edge linework, with most form conveyed by larger value and hue areas.
comparison: The clearest visible difference from original to target is increased modeled-looking thickness and edge curvature, followed by the board segmentation/wear and stronger light separation on fasteners and metal.
The target remains relevant to the original object and palette while exercising the user-authorized freedom to change useful forms, proportions, construction, purposeful decoration and part counts.
Neither original mesh simplicity nor original shader graph structure is treated as an aesthetic lock. The actual gameplay and capture constraints remain to be frozen by the coordinator.
